# CPACC Mastery

> CPACC Mastery is a free study platform for the IAAP Certified Professional
> in Accessibility Core Competencies (CPACC) certification exam. It provides
> study guides, practice tests, and flashcards covering all three CPACC
> exam domains.

The site helps accessibility professionals prepare for the CPACC exam through
structured study content, active recall via flashcards, and practice questions
organized by domain and topic. All content is aligned with the official IAAP
CPACC Body of Knowledge.

The CPACC certification is administered by the International Association of
Accessibility Professionals (IAAP) and validates foundational knowledge in
accessibility core competencies. The exam covers three domains with weighted
importance: Domain 1 (40%), Domain 2 (40%), and Domain 3 (20%).

## Site Structure

The site is organized into three study domains, each containing multiple topics.
Every topic has a dedicated study guide page with detailed content, a flashcard
mode for active recall practice, and quiz functionality for self-assessment.

Main sections:
- Home page: Overview of all domains and navigation
- Practice Test: Mock exam simulating the CPACC certification test
- Domain pages: Overview of each domain with links to individual topics
- Topic detail pages: In-depth study guides with structured learning content
- Flashcards: Per-topic flashcard decks for active recall
- Quizzes: Topic-specific and domain-wide practice questions

## Features

- Practice Test (https://cpaccmastery.com/cpacc-practice-test): Full mock exam and topic-specific quizzes covering all domains. Includes timed test mode and score tracking.
- Study guides with detailed content for each of the 17 CPACC topics, including learning objectives, key concepts, and exam-focused takeaways.
- Flashcards for active recall study, available per-topic.
- Text-to-speech for audio learning, allowing users to listen to study content.
- Dark mode support for comfortable studying in any lighting condition.
- Mobile-responsive design for studying on any device.

---

## Domain 1: Disabilities, Challenges & Assistive Technologies

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/disabilities-challenges-assistive-technology

This domain covers 40% of the CPACC exam. It focuses on understanding
disability from multiple perspectives, knowing the different types of
disabilities and their associated barriers, assistive technologies,
demographic data, and appropriate interaction etiquette.

### Topic 1A: Theoretical Models of Disability

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/disabilities-challenges-assistive-technology/1a-theoretical-models

Study the various theoretical frameworks and models used to understand
disability, including medical, social, and biopsychosocial models.

Key concepts covered:
- Medical model: Views disability as located in the individual's body/mind, focusing on medical intervention and "fixing" the person. Strengths include valuing healthcare; weaknesses include treating disability as a personal defect.
- Social model: Disability is caused by societal barriers, not individual conditions. The foundation of accessibility and human rights approaches. Focuses on removing environmental barriers.
- Biopsychosocial model: Combines biological, psychological, and social factors. Used by the WHO in the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF).
- Human rights model: Extends the social model by framing disability as a human rights issue. Closely aligned with the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD).
- Economic model: Views disability through the lens of economic productivity and cost-benefit analysis.
- Charity model: Portrays people with disabilities as objects of pity needing help, which can be disempowering.
- How different models influence policy, design decisions, and attitudes toward disability.

### Topic 1B: Categories & Characteristics of Disabilities

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/disabilities-challenges-assistive-technology/1b-categories-characteristics

Learn about different disability categories, their characteristics, common
barriers faced by people with disabilities, and effective solutions to
overcome these barriers.

Key concepts covered:
- Visual disabilities: Blindness, low vision, colour blindness. Barriers include inaccessible images, poor contrast, reliance on visual-only information.
- Auditory disabilities: Deafness, hard of hearing. Barriers include audio-only content, lack of captions or sign language interpretation.
- Motor/physical disabilities: Paralysis, limb differences, tremors, chronic pain. Barriers include inaccessible physical spaces, mouse-only interfaces.
- Cognitive and learning disabilities: Intellectual disabilities, learning disabilities, ADHD, autism spectrum. Barriers include complex language, cluttered interfaces, time limits.
- Speech disabilities: Stuttering, apraxia, mutism. Barriers include voice-only interfaces, telephone-only communication.
- Neurological disabilities: Epilepsy, multiple sclerosis. Barriers include flashing content, fatigue-inducing interfaces.
- Psychosocial disabilities: Mental health conditions including depression, anxiety, PTSD. Barriers include stressful interfaces, lack of predictability.
- Multiple/compound disabilities: Combinations of disability types requiring intersectional solutions.
- Temporary and situational disabilities: How disability can be temporary or situational, broadening the understanding of who benefits from accessibility.

### Topic 1C: Assistive Technologies & Adaptive Strategies

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/disabilities-challenges-assistive-technology/1c-assistive-technologies

Explore assistive technologies and adaptive strategies that enable people
with disabilities to perform tasks and access information more effectively.

Key concepts covered:
- Screen readers: Software that reads digital content aloud (JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver).
- Screen magnification: Tools that enlarge screen content for users with low vision.
- Alternative input devices: Switch devices, eye tracking, voice recognition, sip-and-puff devices.
- Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC): Devices and systems for people with speech disabilities.
- Hearing assistive technology: Hearing aids, cochlear implants, FM systems, captioning.
- Mobility aids: Wheelchairs, prosthetics, adaptive controllers.
- Cognitive aids: Text-to-speech, simplified interfaces, memory aids, scheduling tools.
- Adaptive strategies: Techniques people use alongside or instead of technology, such as keyboard navigation, voice commands, or modified workflows.

### Topic 1D: Disability Demographics and Statistics

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/disabilities-challenges-assistive-technology/1d-demographics-statistics

Understand the statistical data and demographic information related to
disabilities worldwide and how this impacts accessibility considerations.

Key concepts covered:
- Global prevalence: WHO estimates that approximately 16% of the global population (1.3 billion people) experience significant disability.
- Age-related trends: Disability rates increase significantly with age; aging populations mean growing demand for accessibility.
- Intersectionality: How disability intersects with gender, poverty, ethnicity, and geographic location.
- Employment gaps: People with disabilities face significantly higher unemployment rates globally.
- Digital divide: Disparities in access to technology and the internet for people with disabilities.
- Why demographics matter for accessibility planning and business cases.

### Topic 1E: Disability Etiquette

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/disabilities-challenges-assistive-technology/1e-disability-etiquette

Master the appropriate language, behaviors, and interactions when working
with or communicating about people with disabilities.

Key concepts covered:
- Person-first vs identity-first language: When to use "person with a disability" vs "disabled person" and respecting individual preferences.
- Respectful communication: Speaking directly to the person, not their companion or interpreter.
- Physical etiquette: Not touching mobility devices or service animals without permission.
- Offering assistance: Ask before helping; respect the answer if declined.
- Avoiding assumptions: Not assuming what someone can or cannot do based on appearance.
- Inclusive event planning: Ensuring meetings, events, and communications are accessible.
- Language to avoid: Outdated or offensive terminology and why it matters.

---

## Domain 2: Accessibility & Universal Design

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/accessibility-universal-design

This domain covers 40% of the CPACC exam. It focuses on understanding
the principles and benefits of accessibility and universal design across
digital, physical, and educational environments.

### Topic 2A: Individual Accommodations vs Universal Design

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/accessibility-universal-design/2a-accommodations-universal-design

Understand the difference between providing individual accommodations and
implementing universal design principles that benefit everyone.

Key concepts covered:
- Individual accommodations: Reactive, person-specific adjustments made after a barrier is identified. Examples include providing a sign language interpreter or a modified workstation.
- Universal design: Proactive approach to designing products and environments usable by the widest range of people without adaptation. Benefits everyone, not just people with disabilities.
- Cost comparison: Universal design is typically more cost-effective when implemented from the start vs retrofitting accommodations.
- Legal obligations: Many jurisdictions require both reasonable accommodations and proactive accessibility.
- The spectrum between accommodation and universal design, and when each approach is appropriate.

### Topic 2B: Benefits of Accessibility

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/accessibility-universal-design/2b-benefits-accessibility

Learn about the wide-ranging benefits of accessibility for individuals,
organizations, and society as a whole.

Key concepts covered:
- Legal compliance: Meeting regulatory requirements and avoiding litigation.
- Market expansion: Reaching the estimated 1.3 billion people with disabilities globally, plus aging populations.
- Innovation driver: Accessibility features often become mainstream innovations (e.g., curb cuts, voice assistants, captions).
- SEO benefits: Accessible websites tend to perform better in search rankings due to semantic HTML, alt text, and structured content.
- Brand reputation: Demonstrating commitment to inclusion and social responsibility.
- Employee productivity: Accessible workplaces benefit all employees, including those with temporary or situational limitations.
- Curb-cut effect: How features designed for accessibility benefit a much wider population.

### Topic 2C: Web Accessibility Principles (WCAG)

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/accessibility-universal-design/2c-wcag-principles

Study the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) principles:
Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust (POUR).

Key concepts covered:
- WCAG overview: Published by the W3C Web Accessibility Initiative (WAI). Current version is WCAG 2.2, with WCAG 3.0 in development.
- Perceivable: Information must be presentable in ways users can perceive. Includes text alternatives, captions, adaptable content, and distinguishable content.
- Operable: Interface components must be operable. Includes keyboard accessibility, sufficient time, seizure prevention, and navigability.
- Understandable: Information and UI operation must be understandable. Includes readable text, predictable behavior, and input assistance.
- Robust: Content must be robust enough for interpretation by assistive technologies. Includes proper parsing and name/role/value.
- Conformance levels: Level A (minimum), Level AA (recommended standard), Level AAA (highest).
- How WCAG is referenced in laws and standards worldwide.

### Topic 2D: Built Environment Accessibility

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/accessibility-universal-design/2d-built-environment

Explore accessibility principles for physical spaces, buildings, and
infrastructure to ensure barrier-free access.

Key concepts covered:
- Physical accessibility: Ramps, elevators, accessible parking, doorway widths, and clear floor space.
- Wayfinding: Signage, tactile indicators, audible signals, and logical layouts for navigation.
- Sensory environment: Lighting, acoustics, and reducing sensory overload.
- Emergency evacuation: Accessible egress routes, visual and auditory alarms, areas of refuge.
- Standards: ADA Standards for Accessible Design, ISO 21542, and local building codes.
- Intersection of built environment and digital accessibility (e.g., accessible kiosks, digital wayfinding).

### Topic 2E: Principles of Universal Design

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/accessibility-universal-design/2e-universal-design-principles

Master the seven principles of universal design and how they can be
applied to create inclusive products and environments.

Key concepts covered:
- Principle 1 - Equitable Use: Design is useful and marketable to people with diverse abilities.
- Principle 2 - Flexibility in Use: Design accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities.
- Principle 3 - Simple and Intuitive Use: Design is easy to understand, regardless of experience, knowledge, language, or concentration level.
- Principle 4 - Perceptible Information: Design communicates necessary information effectively regardless of ambient conditions or user's sensory abilities.
- Principle 5 - Tolerance for Error: Design minimizes hazards and adverse consequences of accidental or unintended actions.
- Principle 6 - Low Physical Effort: Design can be used efficiently and comfortably with minimum fatigue.
- Principle 7 - Size and Space for Approach and Use: Appropriate size and space for approach, reach, manipulation, and use regardless of body size, posture, or mobility.
- Developed at North Carolina State University by Ronald Mace and colleagues.

### Topic 2F: Universal Design for Learning (UDL) + UX

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/accessibility-universal-design/2f-udl-ux

Learn how Universal Design for Learning principles can be integrated with
user experience design to create accessible educational materials and
digital products.

Key concepts covered:
- UDL framework: Developed by CAST (Center for Applied Special Technology). Based on neuroscience research about how people learn.
- Multiple means of engagement: Providing options for recruiting interest, sustaining effort, and self-regulation (the "why" of learning).
- Multiple means of representation: Presenting information in multiple formats and modalities (the "what" of learning).
- Multiple means of action and expression: Allowing diverse ways to demonstrate knowledge (the "how" of learning).
- UX and accessibility: How UDL principles align with accessible user experience design practices.
- Practical application: Designing digital learning experiences that work for all learners.

---

## Domain 3: Standards, Laws & Management Strategies

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/standards-laws-management-strategies

This domain covers 20% of the CPACC exam. It focuses on understanding the
legal and regulatory landscape of accessibility, from international
conventions to national laws, and strategies for integrating accessibility
into organizations.

### Topic 3A: International Declarations and Conventions

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/standards-laws-management-strategies/3a-international-conventions

Study international treaties, declarations, and conventions related to
disability rights, including the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons
with Disabilities.

Key concepts covered:
- Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR): 1948 foundation for human rights, including non-discrimination.
- UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD): 2006 treaty specifically addressing disability rights. Key articles covering accessibility, independent living, education, employment.
- Optional Protocol to the CRPD: Allows individuals to file complaints to the CRPD Committee.
- Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): How disability inclusion connects to global development targets.
- International Labour Organization (ILO) conventions related to disability and employment.
- Marrakesh Treaty: Facilitates access to published works for persons with visual impairments.

### Topic 3B: Regional Instruments on Human & Disability Rights

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/standards-laws-management-strategies/3b-regional-instruments

Learn about regional agreements and instruments that protect the rights
of people with disabilities in different parts of the world.

Key concepts covered:
- European instruments: European Accessibility Act (EAA), European Disability Strategy, EN 301 549 standard.
- Americas: Inter-American Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Persons with Disabilities.
- Africa: African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights, Protocol to the African Charter on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
- Asia-Pacific: Incheon Strategy for Asian and Pacific Decade of Persons with Disabilities.
- How regional instruments complement and implement international conventions.

### Topic 3C: National & Provincial Instruments

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/standards-laws-management-strategies/3c-national-provincial

Understand national and provincial laws, regulations, and policies that
govern accessibility and disability rights.

Key concepts covered:
- United States: Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, 21st Century Communications and Video Accessibility Act.
- European Union: European Accessibility Act, Web Accessibility Directive.
- United Kingdom: Equality Act 2010, Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations.
- Canada: Accessible Canada Act, provincial accessibility legislation (AODA in Ontario).
- Australia: Disability Discrimination Act (DDA).
- Other national frameworks and their approaches to accessibility legislation.

### Topic 3D: Domain-specific & Government Procurement Laws

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/standards-laws-management-strategies/3d-procurement-laws

Explore domain-specific accessibility requirements and government
procurement laws that mandate accessible products and services.

Key concepts covered:
- Section 508 (US): Federal procurement standard requiring accessible ICT.
- EN 301 549 (EU): European standard for ICT accessibility in public procurement.
- Government procurement as a lever for accessibility: How purchasing requirements drive market change.
- Domain-specific regulations: Healthcare, education, transportation, telecommunications, and financial services.
- Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) and Accessibility Conformance Reports (ACR).

### Topic 3E: Applying Accessibility Standards & Regulations to ICT

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/standards-laws-management-strategies/3e-ict-standards

Learn how to apply accessibility standards and regulations to Information
and Communication Technology (ICT) products and services.

Key concepts covered:
- WCAG and its role in legislation: How WCAG is referenced in laws globally.
- ATAG (Authoring Tool Accessibility Guidelines): Ensuring tools that create content produce accessible output.
- UAAG (User Agent Accessibility Guidelines): Standards for browsers and media players.
- EN 301 549: European ICT accessibility requirements and their alignment with WCAG.
- PDF accessibility: PDF/UA standard for accessible documents.
- Mobile accessibility: Applying accessibility standards to mobile applications.
- Testing methodologies: Manual testing, automated testing, and user testing with people with disabilities.

### Topic 3F: Integrating ICT Accessibility Across the Organisation

URL: https://cpaccmastery.com/standards-laws-management-strategies/3f-integrating-ict

Understand strategies for embedding ICT accessibility throughout an
organization's policies, processes, and culture.

Key concepts covered:
- Accessibility maturity models: Frameworks for assessing and improving organizational accessibility capability.
- Policy development: Creating and implementing accessibility policies.
- Roles and responsibilities: Defining who is accountable for accessibility across the organization.
- Training and awareness: Building accessibility skills and culture organization-wide.
- Procurement integration: Including accessibility requirements in purchasing decisions.
- Development lifecycle: Integrating accessibility into design, development, testing, and deployment processes.
- Monitoring and reporting: Tracking accessibility compliance and progress over time.
- Business case: Building the case for organizational investment in accessibility.
